title: Jerusalem’s walls had been broken for decades.
paragraphs: Jerusalem’s walls had been broken for decades.
The city that once symbolized God’s presence now stood exposed, vulnerable, and humiliated.
Many people knew about the destruction.
But only one man allowed it to break his heart.
When Nehemiah heard the news, he did not react with criticism.
He reacted with burden.

He wept.
He prayed.
He fasted.
Because the people God uses to rebuild broken things are often the ones who feel the pain most deeply.
And that is the first lesson.
Burden is often the birthplace of calling.
Nehemiah then did something remarkable.
He left the comfort of the palace to rebuild the ruins of a city.

And the moment the rebuilding started…
Opposition showed up.

Mockery.
Threats.
Plots to stop the work.
Because every time something broken starts being restored, resistance rises.
But Nehemiah refused to come down from the wall.
His answer to distraction was simple:
"I am doing a great work and cannot come down."
Those words still speak today.
Some walls in life are broken:
families
faith
integrity
purpose
communities
And many people see the damage.
Few people pick up stones.
But God is still looking for modern Nehemiahs—people who will rebuild what others gave up on.
Because sometimes the greatest calling in your life…
Is rebuilding something broken.
What “broken wall” in your life or community do you feel called to rebuild right now?
